title: Molecular Synthesis Chess Lab
description: A chemistry lab workbench where the chess set (ABeautifulGame) represents molecular compound stations, the WaterBottle serves as the primary solvent reagent dispenser, and the Duck is a quirky lab mascot that acts as a reaction catalyst. The user must drag the WaterBottle to specific chess piece stations in the correct order, activate the Duck catalyst at precise moments, and validate pH and temperature parameters to synthesize a target compound through a multi-step titration sequence.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive 3D chemistry lab. Load three GLB models using GLTFLoader: Duck.glb, ABeautifulGame.glb, and WaterBottle.glb from their paths. Scene setup: place the chess set (ABeautifulGame) centered on a lab bench (a flat box geometry with metallic material) at y=0. Scale it to roughly 2 units wide. Position the WaterBottle to the right side of the bench, scaled appropriately to look like a reagent bottle with a glowing blue emissive outline. Place the Duck on the left side as the lab catalyst mascot, slightly bobbing up and down via sine animation. Camera: perspective at position (0, 4, 6) looking at origin. Add OrbitControls with limited polar angle. Lighting: one directional light simulating overhead lab fluorescents, one warm point light near the Duck, ambient light at 0.3 intensity. Interaction flow (6-8 steps with validation): 1) User clicks WaterBottle to pick it up (raycasting, highlight with outline). 2) Drag WaterBottle over a specific chess piece (king) — validate proximity within 0.5 units — piece glows green, a particle effect simulates bubbling. 3) A UI panel appears showing pH slider (range 1-14); user must set pH to 7.0 ± 0.3 and confirm. 4) Click the Duck to activate catalyst — Duck spins and emits yellow particles. 5) Drag WaterBottle to the queen piece — validate proximity, triggers second reaction with blue particle burst. 6) Temperature slider appears (range 20-200°C); user must set to 100 ± 5°C. 7) Click a Synthesize button — system validates all parameters were set correctly. 8) On success, all chess pieces emit a rainbow glow, Duck quacks (play a short oscillator beep), and a congratulations banner appears. Use an HTML overlay div for sliders, buttons, and status text. Add a step tracker showing current step out of total. Reject out-of-order actions with a red flash warning message.
